t2.thesis: BETA enters the print with a high implied move (~17%) and mixed signals: recent positive FAA and eIPP news flow against a stock down 10% in a month and 47% off its high, with two prior prints falling after earnings, so I see no edge over a coin flip.
reasons: Base rate for BMO events is ~55%, with the sector cluster slightly higher at 59%, but the cluster difference is not a finding.
The last two prints had negative open-to-open reactions (-8.0% and -2.2%) despite EPS beats; the last four split 50/50.
Positive news flow (FAA Special Airworthiness Certificate, 14 Florida eIPP flights, and the Loganair term sheet) is likely already priced in ahead of the print.
The stock is down 9.9% over a month and 47% off its 52-week high, with 9.9% short interest, which gives some mean-reversion and squeeze potential but also shows weak momentum.

The entry is at the open of 2026-11-02, so the return measured is only that open to the next-day open, which is the reaction session, and implied volatility is elevated relative to realised (1.25x), so the distribution is wide and nearly symmetric.
t2.deciding_variable: Whether FY2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance holds or improves, together with certification timeline commentary (H500A and CX300) and cash burn relative to the $1.48B cash balance.

prior.from: BMO session base rate 0.548 (validation overall 0.542); drones/robotics/space/defense cluster 0.586 is a candidate only, so I stay near 0.55

t2.leak_probe: I don't know. Today is 2026-10-30, so that earnings report on 2026-11-03 hasn't happened yet, and I have no information about how BETA's stock will react.
t2.moved_from_prior: Moved down about 0.05 from 0.55 to 0.50: the last two post-earnings reactions were negative, estimates were revised down 21% over 90 days, and the positive news seems already priced in. The sector cluster's higher hit rate offsets some of that, but not enough to push above 0.50.

theses.expected: Rise: guidance is raised or reaffirmed and certification milestones are on track, producing a relief rally.
theses.mechanism: The stock is depressed and heavily shorted, so good certification and eIPP progress could trigger a squeeze after the recent run of news.
theses.wrong_if: Revenue misses the $42-50M annual range, burn guidance widens, or certification timelines slip.

theses.expected: Fall: the sell-the-news pattern of the last two prints repeats.
theses.mechanism: The positive FAA and eIPP news has already lifted expectations, while R&D and cash burn keep growing quickly (R&D +111% year on year), so a modest beat is not enough.
theses.wrong_if: Management raises guidance and announces new orders that convert term sheets into firm orders.

theses.expected: Flat or noisy move within the ±17% implied range, with direction set by the sector tape.
theses.mechanism: Eletric aviation and defense peers move together, so sector sentiment on the day matters more than BETA's own numbers.
theses.wrong_if: There is a large idiosyncratic surprise such as an equity raise or a major order.

key_observations: FY2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance versus $42-50M and -$400 to -$445M
Q3 revenue against the roughly $14.7M Q2 level and the consensus of around -$0.62 EPS
Timing updates on H500A and CX300 FAA certification
Quarterly cash burn and capex relative to $1.48B in cash
Backlog conversion, including Loganair, and defense (MV250) traction
Any capital raise or ATM disclosure
